status: passed with synthetic private stores on macOS
implementation: Initial publication requires two free slots before starting FreshClam or recording a new wait. The pending deletion of a generation reserves its slot until directory sync is confirmed.

The tracked store format initializes its journal only on a newly created private directory. It records the candidate before moving it and durably records switch intent before replacing the current pointer.

Owner CLI listing and selected deletion use the generation ID and a revision bound to the journal, the checked target, and wait and provider state. Cleanup leaves stages, the provider state and the wait untouched.
When the current reference is absent and a generation has unknown publication history, a normal update also stops before creating an attempt or a stage, including in the earlier store format.
regression_checks: Added ten tests and changed the earlier first publication regression to verify that unknown generations are held even below the capacity limit.

Two stopped attempts filled four slots. At four and three occupied slots the update refused with zero engine starts and unchanged wait. Each selected deletion freed exactly one slot, and the next update reached publication with two slots reserved.

An existing directory did not acquire a journal. Candidate and sidecar move interruptions, a recorded switch intent with no reference, failed reference write and read-back, and later loss of the published reference retained the expected protections.

The intact verified reference allowed a later ordinary update to finish the publication record. An unknown generation in the same store stayed protected while an independently verified candidate could be selected.

An actual CLI subprocess listed and selected a single candidate. A stale revision, linked or corrupt content, an active lease and a malformed journal refused selection. The wait, canonical provider data, synchronization file and referenced stage data remained byte-identical during selected cleanup.

An interrupted deletion was retried against surviving file identities and hashes. Parent sync failure retained the slot even after the directory disappeared. The final retry confirmed absence and released exactly one slot.

development_diagnostics: The four-slot regression caught a reused variable that lost an earlier generation record. The recorded generation set now comes from the store inventory.

The deletion retry regression showed that APFS changes the directory link count as a file is removed. The retry compares the directory device, inode, mode and owner, and separately checks each surviving file against its full identity and recorded hash.
limits: Fault probes used synthetic CVD files, engine replies and disk errors. No existing signature store, deadline, provider state or operating system definitions were used or changed.
Native acceptance with signed CVDs and restart fault tests on macOS and Linux remain pending. Windows and the remote CI jobs were outside this local verification.

findings: Reproduced in a synthetic tracked store: after a selected candidate deletion stopped partway, an update stopped with zero engine starts but told the owner to preserve the store. The listing still offered the candidate as deletable, and retrying its deletion allowed the first publication.
The backlog line for the native acceptance said the CVDs were retrieved by native FreshClam without saying that a local test mirror served them, while the record shows no official provider requests.
changes: When the only remaining blocker is an unfinished selected deletion, the update reports that cleanup and asks the owner to list the store and retry it. Unknown or unconfirmed publication still asks the owner to preserve the store.
README in English and Japanese explains the message. A new test covers the message, the unchanged store and wait, zero engine starts, the retried deletion and the first publication.
The backlog line names the local test mirror and zero official provider requests.
review_follow_up.regression: The new test failed on the reviewed commit with the preserve message and passes after the change.

changes: When a selected first-publication deletion already has an intent record, retry synchronizes the parent directory and rechecks the record and publication reference before removal. If synchronization still fails, the files and occupied slot are preserved.

If the provider synchronization record is missing, or its synced hash disagrees with the optional canonical provider.dat file, the first-publication candidate is listed as protected with provider_state_mismatch. Selected deletion rechecks the state under the updater lock. The wait, provider files and referenced stage are preserved.
regression_checks: Both new tests failed before the fix. An injected directory sync failure left the deletion intent visible. A second failure blocked removal and kept the CVDs, verification record, wait and occupied slot. When sync succeeded, the selected deletion ran afterward and released one slot.

A missing canonical file, different canonical bytes, a canonical file whose absence was recorded, and a missing synchronization record each blocked deletion. The old revision was refused and a fresh listing showed the protection reason. The candidate, wait, journal, sync record and source stage were unchanged by the blocked commands, with zero engine starts. With a matching canonical file and synchronization record restored, selected deletion completed.
